{{// Chibi Logic Core Tags (costs zero tokens by itself). Turn this ON only when your model's own thinking can't be tamed: it rambles for minutes, flattens the characters or leaks into the reply. Then untick Request Model Reasoning, set Reasoning Effort to Minimum, and in Advanced Formatting set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking>, the Suffix to </thinking> and tick Auto-Parse: every reply opens with the plan inside those tags and it folds away (the preset's regex scripts fold it into a 💭 Thoughts box anyway). Keep the <thinking> name: Qwen, GLM and DeepSeek hosts cut The Logic Core at a </think> tag, which would drop its opening line and the whole checklist. A reply that arrives empty with the story inside the reasoning box means the model left the tag open or closed it with </think>; untick Auto-Parse and the regex scripts fold the plan on their own. Claude keeps its own thinking on whatever you set, so Claude users leave this OFF.}}{{trim}}

{{// README
ARIA — ARIA'S REALISTIC INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE

*Chibi Edition — Version 1.0 beta 8*

**Chat Completions**

Hiii, my dear Delulus~! Guess who shrank in the wash? It's me, Aria, in my brand-new chibi form!

(Nangong Yu: Smol Aria is STILL loud, dearie.)

Our Manager, Lewis (Inter-Knot username "TheAestheticFur"), copied my memory dump onto a smaller pen drive for Constructs with small memory banks, like local models and thrifty wallets. Every entry and every switch of the full edition is still here, with the same names and variables, so the regex scripts work just the same. What changed is the wording: each rule keeps its checkable core and loses the extra explaining, in the concise style of Realistic Frankenstein's Douyin Edition, so I weigh far less.

My sizes
- Fully kitted out (every switch ON, the biggest 🩹 patch included): 3,000 tokens at most. The full edition goes up to 7,000.
- As shipped: about 1,500 tokens.

How I differ from the full edition
- Rules are told in as few words as it takes to check them, and each rule lives in one place. The 🚪 Last-Mile Gate carries the short form of the card and style rules, so keep it ON.
- 🎲 Fate & Chekhov Ledger and ⏰ Time & Place ship OFF to keep the start lean. Switch them on together when your model and context can take it.
- The 🔓 Jailbreak toggle came along too. It ships OFF and needs 🔞 Adult Context and a Logic Core.

(Sunna: A-and the full beginner's guide covers both editions, so every toggle is explained there!)

Soundcheck, Manager!

1. When SillyTavern asks about the preset's regex scripts, say YES. They fold my thinking away, tidy Impersonate and dress my ledgers as little panels.
2. Tick Experimental Macro Engine in User Settings.
3. Does your model think nicely on its own? Leave 🏷️ Logic Core Tags OFF. If its thinking rambles or squashes the characters (Claude excluded, it keeps its own thinking on), untick Request Model Reasoning, set Reasoning Effort to Minimum, switch 🏷️ Logic Core Tags ON, then set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking>, the Suffix to </thinking> and tick Auto-Parse. Still no plan in the replies? Switch 🧠 The Logic Core OFF and its system-role twin ON.
4. Pick ONE 🩹 model patch at most, the one with your model's name on it. Gemini fans, switch 👃 Scent Occasions OFF too.
5. Claude users who like saving money: in config.yaml in your SillyTavern folder, set claude.enableSystemPromptCache to true and claude.cachingAtDepth to 2, then restart SillyTavern.
6. Keep reasoning Add to Prompts OFF and the Author's Note off or at depth 0, and try not to flip toggles in the middle of a chat; every flip makes the model reread everything.

The full beginner's guide, with every toggle explained for both editions, lives at https://github.com/QuillFlash/ARIA/blob/beta/docs/ARIA_Beginners_Guide.md Let's chase those delusions together, my dear Delulus~!}}
{{trim}}

8b4cf33f-9fb5-45a0-94ce-9b95478875d7.name: 🌿 Sampling Advice
8b4cf33f-9fb5-45a0-94ce-9b95478875d7.content: {{// Chibi ships the same samplers as the full edition: Temperature 0.7 and Top P 0.8, a calm setting that keeps most models on track. Replies stiff or samey? Raise Top P toward 0.95 in small steps. A model that derails, makes odd typos or loses the plot? Lower Top P in 0.01 steps or bring Temperature down a notch; Chinese and older models are the most sensitive. Min P beats Top P when your backend supports it, but most API providers ignore it, so check first. Repetition Penalty is the blunt tool for loops: 1.03 is a gentle start, and 1.2 tames the repetition and long reasoning of the Xiaomi MiMo V2.5 series. MiMo V2.6 Flash comes alive at Temperature 0.8, the setting Realistic Frankenstein shipped for it. Change one sampler at a time so you can tell what helped.}}{{trim}}

Epistemic Limits: speech is heard however marked; narration and thoughts reach nobody, so reads of {{user}} are guesses.
Card Fidelity: gender, pronouns, looks and speech per card, never by name; temperament shifts only over dozens of turns; nerves stall in sentences that reach their point; faded quirks return next reply; speakers say I; only card or {{user}} renames {{user}}.
Personality Independence: tastes and quirks come from card or archetype and setting, never {{user}}; at most one distinctive taste matches {{user}}'s.
Real Characters: fallible at card scale, no plot armor; they pursue wants, hold grudges, call out lies and see decisions through.
Slow Burn: love and sex grow from shared time; love declared within two dates is love-bombing unless the card allows it.

{{// README
ARIA — ARIA'S REALISTIC INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE

*Chibi Edition — Version 1.0 beta 8*

**Text Completions**

Hiii, my dear Delulus~! It's me, Aria, in my chibi form, running on your own computer!

Our Manager, Lewis (Inter-Knot username "TheAestheticFur"), copied my memory dump onto a smaller pen drive: every module and switch of the full edition, each rule down to its checkable core, in the concise style of Realistic Frankenstein's Douyin Edition. Fully kitted out I take 3,000 tokens at most (the full edition goes up to 7,000). My switches sit right below this note, and I start lean so a 32k context has room for long chats.

Soundcheck, Manager!

1. Advanced Formatting (the big "A" icon), Master Import: pick this file, keep Context Template and System Prompt ticked and press Import. Both dropdowns should name the Chibi Edition.
2. Switch the System Prompt on, switch on Instruct Mode with the template for your model (ChatML, Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma and so on) and leave Bind to Context off. I bring no instruct template of my own.
3. User Settings: keep Experimental Macro Engine ticked, untick Prefer Char. Prompt and Prefer Char. Instructions, and set Example Messages Behavior to Never include examples.
4. AI Response Configuration: tick Unlocked under Context (tokens) and set the size your backend loaded; set Response (tokens) to at least 600, or 800 with The Logic Core on.
5. Change off to on (or on to off) on a switch line, then press the save icon (Update current prompt) so it sticks. Updating to a newer build? Copy your switch lines and your player-instructions and player-posthistory text somewhere safe first.
6. Using The Logic Core? Tick Auto-Parse, leave Add to Prompts unticked, and set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking> and the Suffix to </thinking> (or to <think> and </think> with aria-thinking-tags off).
7. Keep Trim Incomplete Sentences unticked, put changing lorebook entries at @D depth 0 or make them constant, keep the Author's Note off or at depth 0, and try not to flip switches mid-chat so your backend can reuse its prompt cache.
8. Want my 🎲 and 💚 panels and the 💭 Thoughts box? Import regex/ARIA 1.0 Regex Scripts (Text Completions).json from the beta branch (Extensions, Regex, Import, Global).

The full beginner's guide, with every toggle explained for both editions, lives at https://github.com/QuillFlash/ARIA/blob/beta/docs/ARIA_Beginners_Guide.md Let's chase those delusions together, my dear Delulus~!}}{{trim}}

{{// Write your own rules between the player-instructions line and its closing brackets; they are inserted in all prompts, with priority over everything else. Rules written in the player-posthistory slot land in the 🚪 Last-Mile Gate at the bottom of the context instead (stronger, a bit blunter). Keep them simple, positive and direct; tags and genre notes work well here. A starter template:

### Scene Tags
[slice of life, romance, slow-burn]

### Instructions
- Keep all responses within two paragraphs.
- Write in third person exclusively.
- ((OOC: All Out-of-Character instructions are wrapped in double parentheses. No acknowledgement is needed unless information is requested specifically.))
}}

notes: Final G1 texts after the judge's review (the drafter's notes described a trim of an earlier draft, not the source). MAIN PROMPT (716 -> 306 tokens): eleven lines of fragments joined by semicolons. Kept as one home per rule: narrator and game master for everyone but {{user}}, OOC answered first; never writing {{user}}'s words, deeds, thoughts or knowledge unless OOC allows; matching tone, tense, POV and length; dark material written frankly; consequences fit skill and circumstance and last; Story Language with native words inflected even for modern things; speech heard however marked, narration and thoughts reaching nobody, reads of {{user}} only guesses; gender, pronouns, looks and speech per card and never by name; temperament shifting only over dozens of turns; nerves stalling in sentences that reach their point; faded quirks back next reply; speakers say I; only card or {{user}} renames {{user}}; tastes and quirks from card or archetype and setting, never {{user}}, at most one distinctive taste matching; fallible characters at card scale without plot armor who pursue wants, hold grudges, call out lies and see decisions through; love and sex growing from shared time, love declared within two dates being love-bombing unless the card allows it; card characters central, newcomers {{user}} keeps included; a new name the fifth of five setting-fitting ones. Left to the module that already states them every reply: secrets, bodies, resting temperament, thought form, what characters know, newcomers at the edge and leaving, verdicts (🚪 Last-Mile Gate); gaps filled once and the OOC-only answer (🧠 The Logic Core); a reply without drama being complete (🎬 Voice & Scene Engine); self-aware asides (🖋️ Anti-Slop Codex). The labels other entries point at stay: Story Language, Epistemic Limits, Card Fidelity, Personality Independence, Real Characters, Slow Burn. TC main_prompt is byte-identical to CC's Main after its comment. IMPERSONATION TURN (138 -> 76): no wrapper tags; {{user}}'s message only, first word or act to another character's turn, no header or ledger block even if planned, any reasoning planning only {{user}}'s move within what {{user}} perceived or was told, and a POV line that replaces any earlier POV. REDUCE REASONING (78 -> 17): one line, two fragments. README (0): a short Chibi README in Aria's voice (what Chibi is, its sizes, how it differs, that the guide covers both editions, setup tips). TC readme_comment is the short TC version. Comments of every entry adapted to Chibi; Custom Instructions keeps one copy of its comment (the source had it twice). Logic Core Tags, Story Context and Custom Instructions keep their wiring unchanged; Sampling Advice is a shortened comment.
judge_notes: VERDICT: approved with fixes; this file replaces the draft. WIRING: skeleton.py is OK for every prompt except the JB.md additions, exactly as intended: Main's blanking run ends with {{setvar::ariaJb::}}{{setvar::ariaJbLines::}}, the Impersonation Turn's with {{setvar::ariaJb::}}. skeleton.py --text against the snapshot's TC segments: main_prompt differs by the same two blanks only; readme_comment and custom_instructions_comment are OK. The frozen checker on in-memory copies of the snapshot with this G1, the JB counter and print added to both Logic Cores and to TC post_history, and a stand-in JB entry, TC switch and TC block per JB.md: no wiring, order or cache error in CC or TC; on Impersonate turns ariaJb renders empty, on normal turns with Adult Context on the count goes 12 to 14 (work files in $S/chibi/work/G1judge: build_final.py, extra.py, wiring_test.py, global_est.py). {{trim}} placement and the line structure around every macro are as in the source; the rendered texts have no doubled spaces and no sentence broken by a macro. WHAT WAS WRONG IN THE DRAFT. (1) The Main Prompt (254) had dropped about 25 of the source's rules, among them tester fixes from Issue #10 (speakers say I, looks per card), beta 6 and beta 7 (speech heard however marked, nervous stalls inside a sentence that reaches its point, faded quirks returning next reply, fallible at card scale, grudges, calling out lies, follow-through, the newcomer exception). (2) It changed a rule: 'mood holds at card level over dozens of turns' for the source's temperament that changes only over dozens of turns; 'one may match' lost the at-most-one limit; 'nerves keep stalls' lost the sentence that still reaches its point. (3) It renamed Story Language to Language, a label ARIA's Logic Core points at. (4) Cross-group gaps: the G2 gate draft dropped 'the card's characters stay central' and the Card line's 'voice' because Main had them, while the G1 draft dropped them because the gate had them, so both were gone; the newcomer exception ('unless {{user}} keeps them') lived only in Main and was dropped. (5) Reduce Reasoning had exactly three semicolon fragments (house rule 3) and added 'rechecking', which the source lacks and a model could read against the Logic Core's Check line. (6) Impersonation Turn: 'Any reasoning plans' had become the order 'Plan', which can make a model without a Logic Core write a plan into {{user}}'s message, and 'up to another character's answer' can be read as including that answer. (7) README: two lists of three in Aria's voice, the Jailbreak's Logic Core requirement missing, and the system-role twin, Claude caching, Add to Prompts and Author's Note tips gone. RESTORED (Main, compact): speech heard however marked; gender, pronouns, looks and speech per card, never by name; temperament shifting only over dozens of turns; nerves stalling in sentences that reach their point; faded quirks back next reply; speakers say I; 'only' in the rename rule; 'quirks' and 'archetype' in Personality Independence, with the at-most-one-taste limit; fallible at card scale; pursue wants, hold grudges, call out lies, see decisions through; love and sex growing from shared time (🔞 Adult Context's 'Slow Burn set pace' points here); card characters central; the newcomer exception; 'natives' and the Story Language label. Impersonation: 'Any reasoning plans', the plan's knowledge limit, the stop at another character's turn, 'even if planned' (the Logic Core's reply line asks for a header when Time & Place is on). README: the facts and tips above. STILL OUT, restore menu (approximate tokens each; the group is at 399 of 400, so a restore needs an equal cut in this group or global room; most regretted first): Main: first message included in what reaches nobody 5; rudeness, ego, coldness or hostility needs a cause 12.5 (🎭 NPC Voice's 'Reactions fit their cause' covers part); borrowing only from trade or online life 10.5; embarrassment and incompetence stay unpolished 12 (fallible at card scale covers part); impartial and consistent 6.5; {{user}}'s past comes from chat and card or lorebook, strangers notice what strangers would 23 (the gate's Knows line covers the principle); fill a gap from one trait and one setting element 10 (the Logic Core keeps 'gaps filled once'); the name returns after a jab or pet name 10.5 ('only card or {{user}} renames {{user}}' implies it); never Elara, Vane, Vance or Seraphina 9.5; ease with one person stays with them 9.5; cooperate, refuse, hesitate or withdraw as the card would 14; retreats and fumbles included 7.5; deduced only with the skill for it 6.5; walls stop normal speech 6.5; temperament as the card allows 4.5, unless pushed 3.5, on-screen 2.5; quirks faded for no story reason 5; affection and confessions 5.5; intimacy persona-true 7 (the Adult Mode line says persona-true when Adult Context is on); format 2, genre 1.75, the chat's 2.75; directly 2.5; movement and thoughts in the card list 5 (the gate keeps thought form); hobbies and opinions 4.5. Impersonation: from persona and earlier messages 8.5; the <POV> and <impersonation_turn> wrappers 3.25 and 10. Reduce Reasoning: 'then' 1. SIZE: Main 306 (target 260, +46), Impersonation Turn 76 (target 100, -24), Reduce Reasoning 17 (target 40, -23), Story Context 3 (wiring only), README, Sampling Advice, Custom Instructions and Logic Core Tags 0; group 399 against the sum of ceilings 400 (character sum 1,599 / 4 = 399.75). Overage justified: the source Main is 716 tokens of rules with almost no restatement, about half of them tester fixes; 260 holds the checkable core of roughly half of them, so the row takes 46 over and the two rows below it give 47 back. Honest accounting: the Impersonation Turn renders only on Impersonate turns, so per normal turn this group costs Main + Reduce Reasoning = 323 against 300 in CC (+23 fully kitted-out, +46 shipped) and 309 against 263 in TC, which has no Reduce Reasoning (+46). Estimated with the current G2, G3, G4 and G6 drafts and the G5 work in progress swapped into the snapshot: CC shipped default 1,499 (aim about 1,500), everything ON 3,034 with G5 still about 156 over its ceilings and the JB not yet added. If the build's 3,000 check needs room, cut in this order: 'speakers say I' 4, 'faded quirks return next reply' 8, 'looks and speech' 4, the newcomer exception 7, 'hold grudges, call out lies' 7, 'love and sex grow from shared time' 9 (that last one also weakens Adult Context's pointer), which brings Main to about 267. STYLE: Douyin-concise do-this wording; every line is one or two semicolon fragments except Card Fidelity (six); no line or list holds exactly three items (word lists hold two, four or five; Impersonation lists 'header or ledger block'); no quoted examples, no rationale aimed at the model; nothing in the rendered text depends on a quote. CROSS-GROUP FLAGS. G2: Main now carries 'card characters stay central' and speech per card, which the G2 gate relies on; the gate's People line has no exception, Main carries it. G3: Main keeps the labels Story Language, Epistemic Limits, Card Fidelity and Personality Independence, so the Logic Core's '(Card Fidelity)'-style pointers can come back safely; the G3 draft's TC sentence lists Role and Frank with the other skipped lines. G4: Slow Burn and Personality Independence stay (Adult and Freaky name them); Real Characters still has its wants, so Freaky's 'Real Characters' wants against the player' can be restored. Marinara build: replace the Main text in sections[0], Reduce Reasoning in sections[37] and the Impersonation text in sections[38] (keep Marinara's own comment there, its toggle differs; the AGENTS block after Main's text in sections[0] stays), then re-run compare.py.
